title: Ebola Outbreak: Current Situation - Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | CDC (.gov)

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-31. Event date: August 4, 2026, as referenced in the outbreak overview.
analysis.location_and_population: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. In DRC, cases confirmed in Haut-Uele, Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, and Tshopo provinces. In Uganda, cases diagnosed in Kampala.
analysis.event: CDC is responding to an outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in remote areas of DRC and Uganda. This is the 17th outbreak of Ebola in DRC and is spreading substantially faster than previous outbreaks.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Over 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of response activation, surpassing the 2018 DRC outbreak which took 235 days to reach 1,000 cases. More than 100 fatalities reported in the first week of July. No cases confirmed in the United States. The overall risk to the American public and travelers remains low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Response is challenging due to ongoing conflict, security issues, lack of trust in government, and misinformation, which complicate contact tracing and infection control. analysis.brief_en: The CDC is responding to a rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. This is the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC and has already surpassed 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days, making it the second-largest outbreak on record and significantly faster than previous outbreaks. Cases have been confirmed in multiple provinces in DRC, including Haut-Uele, Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, and Tshopo, while all cases in Uganda have been diagnosed in Kampala with no community spread reported. The outbreak has resulted in over 100 fatalities in early July. Despite the rapid spread, the risk to the American public remains low, with no cases confirmed in the United States. The response faces challenges due to ongoing conflict, security issues, and misinformation in the region.

title: Scientists advance Sudan Ebola vaccine development

analysis.location_and_population: Development efforts are global, with presentations at the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The target population includes healthcare workers and vulnerable populations in Africa, particularly during outbreaks.

analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No cases, deaths, or exposures reported. The urgency reflects growing concern over increasing Ebola outbreak frequency. Pre-clinical studies showed complete protection in non-human primates, with potential for ring vaccination strategies.

title: Ebola Bundibugyo strain outbreak worst ever in DR Congo, WHO says - BBC

analysis.time: Published on 2026-08-01; outbreak declared on 15 May 2026; highest weekly total reported in the past week with 567 cases and 296 deaths.
analysis.location_and_population: Democratic Republic of Congo, centered in Ituri province (northeast), with spread to North and South Kivu provinces; also 20 cases in Uganda and one in France; two cases treated in Germany.
analysis.event: Confirmed outbreak of Ebola virus disease caused by the Bundibugyo strain, declared as the largest in DR Congo's history by WHO.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 3,605 confirmed cases including 1,587 deaths (44% fatality rate) as of 30 July; surpasses previous 2018-2020 outbreak (nearly 3,500 cases, almost 2,300 deaths); WHO describes transmission as 'intensifying' with 'exceptional pace'.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: No approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo strain; vaccines in development in UK and Singapore; response hampered by insecurity, population displacement, cross-border movement, and M23 armed group presence in affected areas.

analysis.brief_en: The World Health Organization has declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo the largest in the country's history, caused by the Bundibugyo strain. As of 30 July, there are 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths, representing a 44% fatality rate. The outbreak, declared on 15 May 2026, has intensified with the highest weekly total of 567 cases and 296 deaths recently reported. While centered in Ituri province, it has spread to other regions including North and South Kivu, with cases also reported in Uganda, France, and Germany. Response efforts face challenges from insecurity, displacement, and cross-border movements. No approved vaccine or treatment exists for this strain, though development efforts are underway in the UK and Singapore.
